title: Peppermint patties
subtitle: minty fondant centres dipped in dark chocolate with a cool, clean finish
excerpt: Peppermint patties are discs of firm peppermint fondant coated in a thin layer of dark chocolate. The centres are made from icing sugar, egg white, and peppermint extract, shaped into rounds, and chilled before dipping. The result is a clean-tasting sweet with a cool mint centre and a snapping chocolate shell.
sourceNotes: Peppermint patties in this format are most associated with American confectionery, particularly York Peppermint Patties, introduced in 1940. The fondant-and-chocolate format is older, with similar sweets in British confectionery tradition under the name peppermint creams, documented in Mrs Beeton and other household cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a single layer between sheets of baking paper for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. The fondant centres keep refrigerated for 3 days before dipping.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: Peppermint patties are flat rounds of firm mint fondant coated in dark chocolate. The centres need no cooking: icing sugar, egg white, and peppermint extract worked together into a smooth, pliable dough that is rolled out and cut into rounds. The fondant firms up in the fridge before dipping so the chocolate sets cleanly around it.

Beat the egg white lightly with a fork until just broken up. Add the peppermint extract. Sift the icing sugar into a large bowl and make a well in the centre. Add the egg white mixture and work together with a wooden spoon, then by hand, until a smooth, firm dough forms. Add a little more icing sugar if it sticks.
Dust the work surface lightly with icing sugar. Roll the fondant to about 8 mm thick. Cut out rounds with a 4 cm cutter. Re-roll the trimmings and cut again. Place on a tray lined with baking paper.
Refrigerate the fondant rounds for 30 minutes until firm.
Melt the dark chocolate in a bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat.

Drop a fondant round into the melted chocolate. Turn with a fork to coat, lift out, let the excess drip off, and place back on the baking paper. Repeat with all rounds. Refrigerate for 30 minutes until the chocolate shell is fully set.

attrs.problem: Fondant too sticky to roll out
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding too little icing sugar; the dough must be firm enough to hold its shape.
attrs.fix: Dust liberally with icing sugar and knead in a little more until the dough no longer sticks to your hands. Chilling the dough for 10 minutes also helps.

attrs.problem: Chocolate coating cracking or pooling unevenly
attrs.avoid: Avoid dipping fondant centres that are not fully chilled; the warmth causes the chocolate to slide off before it can set.
attrs.fix: Chill the fondant rounds for a full 30 minutes before dipping. Work quickly once the rounds come out of the fridge.
